title: Cold rebuild: find the crashed container
summary: Investigate a broken shop with ps, logs and exec on a real Docker Engine, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *run, ps, logs, exec* you found a crashed container, read its log and looked inside a
running one, on a real Docker Engine. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to
peek at**. The checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The `api` container crashed and shows `Exited (1)`. You run `docker exec -it api sh`. What happens?
options: An error: the container is not running, so there is no process to join
A shell opens inside the stopped container
Docker restarts the container and opens a shell
A shell opens in a fresh container from the same image
steps.explain: `exec` needs a running container. Start with `docker logs api` to see why it exited.

steps.title: Find the crashed container, cold
prompt: A real Docker Engine runs in this terminal with the same small shop: `api`, `worker`, `cache` and `report`.
1. Write the name and exit code of the container that stopped with an error into `~/answers/crashed.txt` (`NAME CODE`).
2. Write the error line it printed into `~/answers/cause.txt`.
3. Write the `max_connections` value from `/etc/shop/api.conf` inside the `api` container into `~/answers/max.txt`.
From memory: no hints this time.
